c.tagline: South India's Dravidian capital of temples, filter coffee, and the world's second-longest urban beach.

taxi.fareNote: Auto-rickshaws rarely use the meter and require firm negotiation before boarding; app cabs (Uber/Ola) and prepaid airport counters give the most predictable, honest fares.

emergency.note: 112 is India's single all-in-one emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance; 100 reaches police directly and 108 is the dedicated ambulance line.

hood_landmark.Nungambakkam: Khader Nawaz Khan Road, Nungambakkam, Chennai

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing at markets and on the beach; touts and taxi/auto overcharging

hood_desc: The historic core along the Marina Beach seafront around Triplicane, home to the Parthasarathy Temple, the Ice House, and cheap lodges; best for first-timers who want to be near the water, temples, and budget eats.

Chennai's frenetic shopping district packed with silk-saree emporiums, jewellery showrooms, and Ranganathan Street's crowds; suits travelers who want retail therapy and are happy amid noise and bustle.

The cultural and spiritual heart around the Kapaleeshwarar Temple, San Thome Basilica, and December music-season sabhas; suits travelers wanting classical arts, heritage, and traditional Tamil Brahmin life.

A leafy, upmarket central area of hotels, consulates, restaurants, and Khader Nawaz Khan Road's boutiques; a convenient, slightly quieter base for business travelers and those wanting dining within walking distance.

A relaxed, affluent southern district stretching toward the East Coast Road (ECR) with cafes, the Theosophical Society gardens, and easy access to Elliot's Beach; suits families and those wanting calm and greenery.

water.note: Tap water is not safe for visitors; use bottled or filtered water, including for brushing teeth.

transit.hours: Chennai Metro runs roughly 4:30 AM to 11:00 PM; suburban and MRTS local trains run from around 4:00 AM to 11:00 PM; city buses run late but night frequency is sparse.
transit.note: Chennai Metro (CMRL) covers key corridors and the airport, complemented by an extensive suburban rail network, the MRTS elevated line, and MTC city buses; auto-rickshaws and app cabs fill the gaps.
transit.pay: Metro uses tokens, QR tickets via app, and the rechargeable Singara Chennai / travel smart card; suburban rail and MTC buses take cash and, increasingly, UPI/QR payments. As of 2026 there is no single card covering all modes.

bus: SETC/state intercity buses from CMBT Koyambedu to other Tamil Nadu and South Indian cities
train: Long-distance rail from Chennai Central and Chennai Egmore stations

transit.m: Chennai Metro Blue Line from Airport station to city center (~40 min)
Suburban rail from Tirusulam station (adjacent to airport) to Beach/Tambaram
Prepaid taxi or app cab to city center (30-45 min)

tip.r: Not expected but appreciated; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants and small tips for hotel staff and drivers is customary for good service.
